messages.subject: Re: Errors in MCDS analyses of aerial survey data
parts:
Hello all,

As promised, here is a summary of the solution to my earlier email. Thank
you to Eric Rexstad for proposing the following resolution. In his words:

" Recognise the tasks you are asking Distance to perform: estimate a
coefficient associated with a couple of sightings to describe how the shape
of the detection function changes when an unusual glare condition occurs.
Given very little information with which to estimate said coefficient,
Distance complains and fails to converge.

My advice (uninformed by your data) is to build a contingency table
(assuming your covariates are discrete rather than continuous) of the
number of sightings by factor combinations. That will shed light on the
magnitude of the 'data sparsity' problem. At that point you might decide
that rather than 3 levels of glare, you recode to only 2 levels.

So the "automatic" nature of 'letting Distance figure it out' begins to
wane; you need to be more elegant in the type of covariate models you
propose and the coding of covariates in your data. So there is no 'magic
bullet' in a covariate analysis."

As he suggested, I built a contingency table and recognized that a few on
my covariate combinations had only 1 sighting. I then recoded the
problematic variable to correct this issue. With the newly recoded
variable, I was able to run each candidate MCDS model individually (not
using automated model selection) to select the best model.

I hope this helps anyone with similar data issues.

Best,
Caitlin


On Thu, Jan 16, 2014 at 12:11 PM, Caitlin Bovery <cmbo...@gmail.com> wrote:

> > Hello all,
> >
> > I'm having some trouble with my MCDS analyses that I'm hoping someonecan
> > shed some light on. I am analyzing the results of a 2-year aerial survey
> > project for where a survey was conducted each month for 2 years in the same
> > area. The main goal of this study is to estimate density by season within
> > years, for example "Spring 2011" (8 strata), to examine changes in density
> > of sea turtles. I have successfully analyzed the dataset using CDS
> > analysis and am fully comfortable with it's function and my results. I fit
> > a pooled detection function to compensate for low sightings in some seasons
> > (winter/fall) and then estimated density by strata. Using model selection
> > to select from all possible models, a hazard-rate model with no adjustments
> > was selected as the best fit model.
> >
> > The next step in my analyses is to incorporate environmental factors
> > (observer, weather, glare, sea state) to determine if MCDS improves the
> > model of the detection function and thereby estimates of density. Here is
> > where I'm encountering problems. I have a few errors that I'm hoping
> > someone can provide some guidance on:
> >
> > 1) ** Warning: Estimation routine failed to converge as could not
> > calculate area under pdf in iteration 9. Using results from previous
> > iteration. ** ** Warning: convergence failure **
> >
> > - I received this error when beginning MCDS analyses. I first tested
> > only the hazard-rate model with no adjustments using all possible covariate
> > combinations. Is it a good idea to use the model selected from CDS? So far
> > I have tried all possible covariate combinations using only this model and
> > very little trouble there. On some of the more complicated models (3 or 4
> > factors) I receive this error though. I'm not sure why the model is not
> > converging. Any suggestions as to how to deal with this?
> >
> > 2) ** Error: Analysis engine terminated unexpectedly (with error code
> > -1073741663).**

> > 0 0 **

> > -- End of Analyis Engine Log File --
> >
> > ** Warning: Analysis engine wrote some output to the console error stream,
> > reproduced below. ** (I've copied the entire log code for this error at
> > the end of the email)
> >
> > - When using automatic model selection in MCDS to asses all possible
> > models (testing half-normal & hazard-rate with cosine & simple polynomial),
> > I'm getting this error with even the most simple models that include only 1
> > covariate and stratifying by season. I tried global models without using
> > stratification and had successful analyses but I do still need seasonal
> > estimates of density. Is there a way to acquire seasonal density estimates
> > using the global models? Or is there something that I've done wrong in my
> > attempts using stratification? The ONLY difference when running the models
> > has been the use of stratification by season - all other parameters were
> > kept the same.
> >
> > I would greatly appreciate any pointers you may have that can help me
